newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper called to open 0.30-0.40-cent higher.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper called to open 0.30-0.40-cent higher.

text.p: COMEX copper futures were called to open higher, holding key support in London of $2,300 a tonne in the three-month contract.
COMEX September was seen opening 0.30-0.40 cents up from Wednesday's close of 106.20 cents a lb, after trading in a 106.20-106.50-cent range in ACCESS trade.

London Metal Exchange stocks increased 800 tonnes in Thursday's report to 245,775 tonnes, continuing a seven-week trend, in which stocks have more than doubled. COMEX copper stocks declined 163 short tons to 31,807 tons.

The LME three-month price fell $15 overnight to $2,308 a tonne at 0735 EDT, but is still holding above $2,300, a psychological support level. The cash-to-three-month backwardation was steady to slightly firmer at $25/$27.

In other news, a report from Peter Hollands' Bloomsbury Minerals Economics attributes the 46,100 tonne increase in LME Singapore stocks over the last seven weeks to a liquidation of China's strategic reserve, not a seasonal slowdown.
Many physical traders have attributed the increase to a combination of Chinese selling, poor seasonal demand, and deliveries against short positions by the South Koreans.
